REGULAR MEETING AGENDA
CITY COUNCIL OF THE CITY OF CERRITOS
AND THE SUCCESSOR AGENCY TO THE CERRITOS REDEVELOPMENT AGENCY
THURSDAY - APRIL 10, 2025 - 07:00 P.M.
CERRITOS CITY COUNCIL CHAMBER
18125 BLOOMFIELD AVENUE, CERRITOS, CA 90703
Agenda Materials
The complete agenda for this meeting is available on-demand at cerritos.gov and at the Office of the City Clerk, 18125 Bloomfield Avenue, 1st floor, Cerritos, CA, during regular business hours (Monday through Friday, 8:00 a.m. to 5:00 p.m., weekend and observed holidays excepted). Any materials submitted to the legislative body after distribution of this agenda will be available for public inspection in the Office of the City Clerk during regular business hours. Requests for agenda materials or meeting participation assistance can also be made by email to city_clerk@cerritos.us or by phone at (562) 916-1248 during regular business hours.
Order of Agenda
The City Council, by majority of those members present, may reorder the business items listed on the agenda.
PUBLIC OBSERVATION AND PARTICIPATION
The public can observe the meeting via livestream on the City’s website at cerritos.gov, on cable television at Cerritos TV3, or in person in the Council Chamber.
Public Comments
Members of the public may provide public comment for this meeting in person at the meeting or in writing as described below.
In-person public comment : Public comment on business agenda items will be opened and may be provided during consideration of that business agenda item. Public comment on Consent Calendar, Closed Session, and non-agenda items will be opened and may be provided during Agenda Item No. 6.
Written public comment (hard copy or email) : Public comment may be submitted via email to city_clerk@cerritos.us or by hard copy to the Office the City Clerk at 18125 Bloomfield Avenue, Cerritos, CA 90703 no later than 3:00 p.m. on the day of the meeting. Please identify the agenda item number in the subject line of the email or hard copy document. All written correspondence received by the 3:00 p.m. deadline will be distributed to the legislative body prior to the meeting and retained with the official meeting record.
Americans with Disabilities Act (ADA) Accommodations
In compliance with the ADA, any person with a disability who requires accommodation in order to participate in a meeting should contact the Office of the City Clerk at (562) 916-1248 or at city_clerk@cerritos.us in advance of the meeting to request accommodation. The City will use its best efforts to provide reasonable accommodations related to the meeting.

Report from City Manager/Executive Director
During this part of the meeting the City Manager/Executive Director or designated staff will have an opportunity to report on various City matters and/or respond verbally to questions or comments from the prior City Council meeting, including any request by the City Council to provide a brief supplemental report or brief follow-up response to items from the prior City Council meeting's agenda.
11B.
City Council Communications/Committee Reports/Meeting Reports
City Council Communications/Committee Reports/Meeting Reports During this part of the meeting members of the City Council report to the community on various matters of interest, including reports concerning committees on which the Councilmembers serve and reports on meetings/conferences attended. In addition, verbal reports will also be provided in such cases where the City Council-appointed delegate and/or alternate is unable to attend a scheduled meeting, and there is insufficient time to schedule an agenda item for Council consideration of another alternate, necessitating a Mayor's urgency appointment. Requests may also be made of staff for reports which will be presented to the City Council at a subsequent meeting, or for the scheduling of future agenda items. There will be no discussion or action taken on any of the items that may be presented during this agenda item, except to approve or ratify travel expenses for City-related business or to cancel or reschedule a City Council public meeting.

MINUTES OF A REGULAR MEETING OF THE CERRITOS CITY COUNCIL AND THE SUCCESSOR
AGENCY TO THE CERRITOS REDEVELOPMENT AGENCY HELD THURSDAY, APRIL 10, 2025, 7:00
PM, IN THE COUNCIL CHAMBER AT CERRITOS CITY HALL, 18125 BLOOMFIELD AVENUE,
CERRITOS, CALIFORNIA.

  1.  Call to Order

  The meeting was called to order at 7:00 p.m.

  2.  Invocation

  The invocation was given by Pastor Rory Corrigan, Church in Cerritos.

  3.  Pledge of Allegiance

  The Pledge of Allegiance was led by Whitney High School Girls Basketball Team.

  4.  Roll Call

  The following members of the City Council/Successor Agency were in attendance:

  Council/Agency Member Jennifer Hong
  Council/Agency Member Mark E. Pulido
  Council/Agency Member Sophia M. Tse
  Mayor Pro Tem/Vice Chair Lynda P. Johnson
  Mayor/Chair Frank Aurelio Yokoyama

  5.  Presentations/Appointments

  5A.  Presentations

  Proclamations were made by the City Council honoring:

  Deputy Nelida Viveros, Deputy Xavier Alvaraez, Deputy Erick Mutum, Deputy Daniel
  Mailloux, Deputy Rebecca Chavez, Law Enforcement Technician Leslie Gutierrez, Julian
  Mata (911 caller), Preston Hoang (911 caller) (Life Saving Rescue of Child).

  Jeffrey Nishida (Rank of Eagle Scout).

  Cerritos Girls Intermediate All-Stars Youth Basketball (Southern California Municipal
  Athletic Federation Open “A” Division Champions).

  Whitney High School Girls Basketball Team (2025 CIF State Division IV Champions).

  6.  Public Comments and Suggestions

  The Mayor opened the public comments period for items not listed on the meeting
  agenda but that were within the subject matter jurisdiction of the City Council, the
  Consent Calendar, and Closed Session.

  Jerry Jenson expressed support for proclamation recipients and the City’s recognition of
  the subject recipients. He also expressed concern regarding fraud committed against the
  senior community and thanked the City for providing notice to residents regarding fraud
  protection.

  Karl Seitz expressed concern regarding graffiti abatement and maintenance efforts at his
  business location.
 City of Cerritos  Thursday, April 10, 2025, 7:00 p.m.
City Council/Successor Agency Regular Meeting  Page 2 of 14

6.  Public Comments and Suggestions (continued)

  Sam Desai expressed support for the five minute public comment time limit and spoke
  regarding various City issues.

  Teddy Lloyd spoke regarding the potential for the Cerritos Center for the Performing Arts
  to work with Anschutz Entertainment Group (AEG).

  Scott Smith, ABC Unified School District (District) representative, spoke regarding current
  recruitment to fill a vacancy on the District’s Board of Education, Trustee Area 5. He also
  thanked the City for its commitment to partnership with the District.

  Daisy Lagasca Denson spoke regarding an upcoming American Cancer Society event and
  submitted documents for the official record. (Documents submitted to the City Council at
  a public meeting are considered public record. Public requests for copies of the full-text
  redacted written correspondence can be made during regular business hours to the Office
  of the City Clerk.)

  Rocky Pavone spoke regarding National Financial Literacy Month and requested the City
  Council reconsider Council appointments for service on external agencies.

  Kirit Chauhan expressed concern regarding protections for the senior community and
  expressed support for the establishment of a Senior Services Committee.

  Gabriel Perales, representative of U.S. Small Business Administration, provided
  information on assistance available for community members and small businesses
  affected by the recent local wildfires.

  Chris Scott expressed concern regarding recent waste hauling fee increases for
  commercial customers.

  Pat Patnaik thanked the City Council for recognizing the heroes involved in the recent
  child rescue and expressed support for the City’s law enforcement agents.

  Fred Sacramento expressed support for the City’s law enforcement agents and the recent
  decline in local crime.

  Jose Amador, Western States Carpenters Union (Union) respresentative, offered
  congratulations to the newly elected Councilmembers and recently selected Mayor and
  Mayor Pro Tem. He also spoke regarding Union collaboration with the City, and the
  Union’s resident membership and submitted a document for the official record.
  (Documents submitted to the City Council at a public meeting are considered public
  record. Public requests for copies of the full-text redacted written correspondence can be
  made during regular business hours to the Office of the City Clerk.)

  Mayor Yokoyama announced that prior to the meeting the Council/Agency members
  received full-text, unredacted copies of the three (3) written comments submitted for
  Item 7D, by the deadline listed on the agenda and for inclusion in the official record.
  Requests for copies of the written comment submitted for this meeting can be made
  during regular business hours to the Office of the City Clerk.

  Seeing no further speakers, the Mayor declared the public comments period closed.

7B.3. Approval of Fiscal Year 2024-25 budget amendments (COUNCIL).

  MOTION: It was moved by Pulido, and seconded by Hong, to authorize an administrative
  initiated Fiscal Year (FY) 2024-25 budget amendment in accordance with Joint Budget
  Resolution No. 2024-12/CSA No. 2024-01 and the Strategic Financial Plan and Budget
  Preparation Policy (Policy 2.04) as adopted by the City Council, as follows:

  Account/Project: 110-552-79070 (Equipment & Machinery)
  Amount: $215,000
  Justification: A budget amendment is requested for $215,000 in additional funding to
  support Phase II of the City’s Automated License Plate Reader (ALPR) camera program.
  Funding for Phase II was originally budgeted in the FY 2024-25 budget. However, due to
  vendor delays, implementation of Phase I extended into the new fiscal year. As a result,
  the Phase II appropriation was used to complete Phase I. Because the funds originally
  allocated for Phase I in FY 2023-24 were not carried over, this amendment is now
  necessary to restore that prior year funding and allow Phase II to proceed as planned.
  This request supports recent City Council direction to enhance public safety and crime
  reduction efforts.

  The motion carried (5 – 0) as follows:

  AYES:  Hong, Pulido, Tse, Johnson, Yokoyama
